Update 2026-09-27: card p08 was answered with a question (DL-126): Jared intended ELI5 as a project-level default with a per-chat toggle, and asked whether that would make the agent send two responses or resend one. The question has to be answered for him and the card re-asked; nothing is compiled. Update 2026-09-27 (lead): the design lead's proposed answer to Jared's question, awaiting his confirmation and NOT compiled: switching ELI5 affects only replies written after the switch; nothing is re-sent or sent twice; an optional on-demand "Explain this reply simply" may re-explain one reply; ELI5 is a project default with a per-chat override. Until Jared confirms, no ELI5 behaviour compiles and the census does not gain an ELI5 disclosure.
answer: Jared confirmed the lead's answer in chat on 2026-09-27: ELI5 has a project default that applies everywhere in the project, and a chat's ELI5 control overrides it for that chat only (chat override, else project default, else app default); switching never re-sends or rewrites an earlier reply; "Explain this reply simply" writes one extra reply only when asked; ELI5 is its own sheet with the quick dot as the one-click on and off; dual copy only in tooltips and help. For this ledger the ELI5 disclosure joins the collaboration view-state census: opening or closing it mints no command, it traces the resolution order with general.interaction.chat-eli5 and general.interaction.eli5-default, and choosing this chat's value dispatches cmd.chat.eli5.set (on, off or inherit) while the project and app levels are Settings transactions. Compiled as a dated addition to CWR-033. The project scope on general.interaction.eli5-default is a Settings follow-up, carried as q-029.

summary: How does a steer sent mid-round reach the participants of a Chat Room round?
detail: DL-112 (card n03, owner instruction) says a mid-round message queues for the next round and may be sent immediately to steer without interrupting. It does not say who receives a steer inside a multi-participant round (the Moderator, the current speaker, or every participant) or what the room's composer says; DL-112 routes this to the lead. CWR-024 compiles the queue and the no-interrupt rule only. Register line B-CW-10 of /mnt/Cursor/PuppetMaster-Evidence/scratch/pm56-modules-canon-20260927/IMPACT-REGISTER.md (SHA-256 71227f8edda108ed849256d909ff12f859f98bef58202ef988f9d3b4e4f8d493).
raised_by: G1 WAIT wave, 2026-09-27 (residual of an answered card)
answer: A message sent with Send now mid-round is delivered into the current round as steering without interrupting: the next participant to speak reads it first and every later speaker in that round sees it. Compiled in CWR-024 and section 6.3.
